title: A5 Discrete Global Grid System
text: a5R provides R bindings A5 pentagonal discrete global grid system (DGGS), powered a5 Rust crate via extendr. A5 partitions Earth’s surface pentagonal cells across 31 resolution levels. Cells equal-area, encoded 64-bit integers, achieve millimetre-level precision finest resolution. full description system, see A5 project page reference implementation Felix Palmer.

Provides functions indexing coordinates cells, traversing cell hierarchy, computing cell boundaries, compacting/uncompacting cell sets. Powered 'a5' Rust crate via 'extendr'.

text: x area specification. One : numeric vector length 4 (c(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax)) interpreted WGS 84 bounding box. geometry handleable wk::wk_handle() (e.g. wk::wkt(), wk::wkb(), sfc, sf, a5_cell). resolution Integer scalar target resolution (0–30).

title: Generate a grid of A5 cells covering an area — a5_grid
text: Grid generation runs entirely Rust. algorithm expands cells 3 resolution levels time (64x expansion) prunes bounding-box overlap step, keeping working set small. intermediate resolutions spatial buffer applied avoid pruning cells whose children straddle target boundary (A5 cells strictly geometrically nested across resolutions). non-bbox geometry inputs, final exact intersection filter (via Rust geo crate) removes cells fall outside target shape. artificial cell count limit imposed. High resolution combined large area can produce large results consume significant memory. addition numeric bounding boxes, x accepts geometry wk::wk_handle() can process, including sf/sfc objects, wk::wkt(), wk::wkb(), a5_cell vectors. Multiple geometries collected GEOMETRYCOLLECTION automatically. Input geometries assumed use WGS 84 (longitude/latitude) coordinates; projected geometries reprojected produce incorrect results. Antimeridian-crossing bounding boxes supported: xmin > xmax numeric input (e.g. c(170, -50, -170, -30)), bbox automatically split two rectangles either side antimeridian. Known limitation: spatial filtering uses planar geometry longitude/latitude coordinates. can produce incomplete results target areas close poles (~88° latitude) touching antimeridian (longitude ±180°), cell boundary polygons accurately represent true spherical coverage. areas, use larger target geometry ensure complete coverage.
